sso.error.failed: {name} did not confirm who you are, so you are not signed in. Try again in a minute, and if it keeps happening, ask the people who run {name}.
sso.error.cancelled: You stopped at {name} before it was finished, so you are not signed in. Press the button again when you are ready.
sso.error.expired: That sign-in was used already, or it took longer than 10 minutes, so we stopped it to be safe. Start again from this page, and allow cookies from this site if it keeps happening.
sso.error.domain: {name} gave us an address that is not at one of your organisation's email domains, so you are not signed in. Ask the people who run {name} which address your login there has.
sso.error.off: We could not reach your organisation's sign-in just now, or it is no longer set up for this address, so nothing happened. Try again in a few minutes, or ask an admin of your team.
sso.error.busy: Too many attempts from here, so we paused sign-ins for a moment. Wait a few minutes and try again.
sso.error.no_email: {name} did not give us a confirmed email address for you, so you are not signed in. Ask the people who run {name} to share your email address with GrowSigning.
sso.error.taken: Another person at {name} is already connected to the GrowSigning login with this address, so you are not signed in. Ask the people who run {name} which of their logins should have your address.

sso.refused.way_back_two_step: The owner's password is a way back in only while two-step login is on, so you are not signed in. Sign in with "Continue with {name} sign-in", then switch two-step login on under Settings, Security.
sso.refused.two_step_off: You own {account}, where everyone signs in through {name}, and your password with two-step login is the way back in if {name} ever breaks, so two-step login stays on and nothing was changed. sso.refused.hand_over: Everyone at your domains signs in through {name}, and the owner's way back in, if it ever breaks, is their password with two-step login. {person} does not have two-step login on, so the account was not handed over. Ask them to switch it on under Settings, Security first.
sso.err.key: An API key cannot change single sign-on. Sign in to the app as an owner or admin and change it under Settings, Security.
sso.err.no_key: This server cannot keep a client secret safely, so single sign-on cannot be set up here. Ask the people who run this server to set FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
sso.err.domain_form: That is not a domain we can check, so nothing was added. Type it like {example}, without @ or a web address.
sso.err.domains_max: An account can claim at most {max} domains, so nothing was added. Remove one you no longer use first.
sso.err.domain_taken: {domain} is claimed by another GrowSigning account, so it was not added. Ask whoever runs your DNS which account that is, or write to us from Help.
sso.err.domain_gone: That domain is no longer on this account. Reload the page to see the domains it has now.
sso.err.use_form: Use for single sign-on is on or off, so nothing was changed. Send use_sso as true or false.
sso.err.issuer_none: Nothing answers at {host} right now, so nothing was saved. Check the issuer address with the people who run your sign-in service.
sso.err.issuer_private: {host} leads to {address}, which is inside a private network, so the issuer cannot be used and nothing was saved. Use the issuer address your sign-in service shows to the internet.
sso.err.issuer_closed: This server is set up for a closed network and does not look up {host}, so nothing was saved. Ask the people who run this server to add {host} to OUTBOUND_ALLOW.
sso.err.issuer_later: We could not check where {host} leads just now, so nothing was saved. Try again in a minute.
sso.err.discovery_address: That issuer is not an https address, so nothing was saved. Copy it from your sign-in service, like {example}.
sso.err.discovery_unreachable: We could not reach the issuer just now, so nothing was saved. Check the address and try again in a minute.
sso.err.discovery_not_openid: The issuer did not answer as an OpenID Connect service, so nothing was saved. Check that the address is the issuer, not the page where people sign in.
sso.err.discovery_issuer_differs: The service names a different issuer than the one you typed, so nothing was saved. Copy the issuer exactly as your sign-in service shows it.
sso.err.discovery_insecure: The service gives an address that is not https, so nothing was saved. Ask the people who run it to use https for every address.
sso.err.discovery_no_pkce: The service does not offer PKCE with S256, which keeps sign-ins safe, so nothing was saved. Ask the people who run it to switch it on.

sso.err.name_form: That name cannot be used, so nothing was saved. Give a name of 1 to {max} characters, like the name of your organisation.
sso.err.issuer_form: That issuer is not an https address, so nothing was saved. Copy it from your sign-in service, like {example}.
sso.err.client_id_form: That client id cannot be used, so nothing was saved. Copy it from your sign-in service, without spaces.
sso.err.secret_needed: A client secret is needed, so nothing was saved. Copy it from your sign-in service.
sso.err.secret_form: That client secret is too long, so nothing was saved. Copy it again from your sign-in service.
sso.err.enforced_change: Everyone at your domains signs in through {name} now, so its issuer and client id cannot change, and nothing was saved. Switch that off first, change them, try a sign-in, then switch it on again.
sso.err.no_service: No sign-in service is set up for this account. Add one under Settings, Security, Single sign-on.
sso.err.switch_form: These switches are on or off, so nothing was changed. Send enforce and join_new as true or false.
sso.err.try_first: {name} has not been tried yet, so nothing was switched on. Press "Try a sign-in" first and sign in there.
sso.err.no_domain: None of your domains is shown to be yours and set to use single sign-on yet, so nothing was switched on. Add a domain and its DNS line first.

saml.why.unsigned: The sign-in did not work, because the assertion in the identity provider's answer had no valid signature. In your identity provider, choose to sign the assertion (often called "Sign assertion" or "Sign response and assertion"), check that the metadata saved here is current, then try again.
saml.why.issuer: The sign-in did not work, because the answer came from a different identity provider than the metadata saved here. Paste the metadata of the identity provider you are using, then try again.
saml.why.recipient: The sign-in did not work, because the answer was not addressed to our reply address, or it answered an older try. In your identity provider, set the reply address (ACS) to exactly the one shown below, then try again.
saml.why.audience: The sign-in did not work, because the answer was meant for another app. In your identity provider, set the entity ID (sometimes called Audience URI) to exactly the one shown below, then try again.
saml.why.no_email: The sign-in did not work, because the answer did not include the person's email address. In your identity provider, send the email address as an attribute named "email" or as the NameID, then try again.
saml.why.clock: The sign-in did not work, because the times in the answer were out of date or in the future. Check that the clock of your identity provider's server is right, then try again.
saml.why.refused: The sign-in did not work, because your identity provider said no. Check that your own login there is assigned to GrowSigning, then try again.
saml.why.other: The sign-in did not work, because the identity provider's answer could not be checked. Check that the metadata saved here is current and that the answer is signed, then try again.

forms.title: Forms
forms.lede: A public link anyone can open to fill in and sign a template. Put it on your website or in an email, or print its QR code for a poster or a front desk.
forms.only_yours: Only templates you may change are listed here. A form sends in the name of the person its template belongs to, so a colleague’s template can be published by that colleague, by an admin, or by someone they let change it. To make a form from one yourself, copy the template on the Templates page first.
forms.shared: People fill this in on a shared device or in one office (a tablet at the front desk, a classroom, an event)
forms.anyone: Anyone with this link can fill it in and sign. Each person who signs uses one of your signatures.
forms.how_body: The template needs exactly one open signer role. That is the person who fills in the form. When every field they fill in has a label, the fields are asked as questions, one at a time, and then they see the whole document with their answers in it and sign it. Nothing is made or sent until they press the button to go on to sign, and no signature is used until they sign. From one internet connection, an ordinary form allows {open} unfinished starts at a time, ordinary forms together take {hour} starts an hour, and an abandoned start is cleared after a day. A shared-device form allows {shared_open} unfinished starts at a time and {shared_hour} starts an hour from one connection, clears an abandoned one after an hour, and offers "start a new form for the next person" when someone has finished. Whoever comes back to a start that was cleared is offered a fresh form, and you are not emailed about it. While the daily limit for new accounts applies to you (see {link}), each form takes that many new people a day, counted for the form alone: strangers who fill it in never use up what you can send yourself. If someone reports a document they got through a form, a person looks at it, but it does not count towards pausing your account.
